score.notes: A confident Mughal/Taj-grammar facade with genuine end-to-end intent: tripartite base→body→crown, perfect bilateral symmetry, a recessed pointed-arch pishtaq on axis, and two clean registers of gold-framed arched windows flanking it. The teal-dominant / gold-accent / white-pivot palette with a red-and-white striped plinth arcade is disciplined and harmonious — the scheme is the building's identity, and it firmly clears the 'colorful, not monochrome' bar. Detail is rich and purposeful (dome ribs and finial, gold string-courses, dentil banding, the arcaded base) though the broad teal wall panels between window bays stay fairly flat, so it is not whole-facade resolved. Two named, easy improvements keep it short of exceptional: the bulbous dome reads slightly oversized/heavy for the drum, and the four corner minarets are stubby relative to the body, weakening the vertical crown. Clear entrance, strong temple presence, unmistakable but just short of iconic — strong across the board.
